text:
alex: Hey — quick sanity check. I'm landing a TF change that creates private subnets, route tables, and an interface VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) for an internal service. On apply the endpoint resource tries to create ENIs in the subnet before the route table association exists and we get intermittent "subnet not found"/ENI attach errors.

Here's the simplified snippet from the module:

```hcl
resource "aws_subnet" "private" {
  vpc_id = aws_vpc.main.id
  cidr_block = cidrsubnet(var.vpc_cidr, 8, var.az_index)
  tags = { Name = "private-${var.az_index}" }
}

resource "aws_route_table" "private" {
  vpc_id = aws_vpc.main.id
}

resource "aws_route_table_association" "priv_assoc" {
  subnet_id = aws_subnet.private.id
  route_table_id = aws_route_table.private.id
}

resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "svc" {
  vpc_id = aws_vpc.main.id
  service_name = var.service_name
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  subnet_ids = [aws_subnet.private.id]
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.endpoint.id]
}
```

Is adding depends_on = [aws_route_table_association.priv_assoc] on the aws_vpc_endpoint acceptable? Or is there a cleaner pattern (module ordering, target applies, lifecycle blocks) to avoid this race in CI? I'm trying to avoid a two-step apply in the pipeline if possible.

mira: referencing subnet.id should normally make Terraform create the subnet first, but the route_table_association is a separate resource and can be created in parallel. Interface endpoints attach ENIs into the subnet and sometimes race with route-table provisioning on the cloud side. depends_on on the endpoint pointing to the association is the simplest fix:

```hcl
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "svc" {
  # ...
  depends_on = [aws_route_table_association.priv_assoc]
}
```

That forces the endpoint create to wait. Alternatively, move the association into the same module so ordering is implicit, or combine subnet + assoc into a single resource pattern.

sam.k: +1 for depends_on as a quick fix, but fyi we try to avoid cross-module depends_on. If this is split across modules, prefer one of:
- create route tables/assocs in a dedicated networking apply (pre-apply step), then apply workloads
- make the endpoint creation live in the same networking module
- use `terraform apply -target` for the assoc in CI before full apply (ugly but practical)

For production I'd do a two-step deploy: network infra first, then endpoints/services. Keeps plan/apply simpler and reduces blast radius.

jordan: note that interface endpoints create ENIs + SG attachments. We also hit issues before where the SG didn't exist in time (race on SG creation). If you add depends_on, include both the route_table_association and security group resources if they live in other modules. Also tag the subnet ENIs so it's easier to debug.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Staging apply queued at 02:00 UTC. If you need a manual preflight, add a pre-apply target or delay.

alex: Thanks all — I'll add depends_on for the assoc (and SG if needed) to unblock the short-term apply and file a follow-up to move route table assocs into the networking module. Will update the PR with the snippet and a note for CI pre-apply.

sam.k: Sounds good. If you want, I can add a small Jenkins job to run `terraform apply -target=module.network.aws_route_table_association.priv_assoc` as a preflight.

alex: That would help — will ping offline. :thumbsup:
